takeaways: Ports enable many applications to share a single IP address.
UDP offers low latency but no reliability guarantees.
TCP guarantees ordered, lossless delivery using sequence numbers and acknowledgments.
The three‑way handshake prevents old duplicate connections from being mistaken as new.
Sliding‑window flow control matches the sender’s rate to the receiver’s buffer capacity.
Congestion control protects the network by adjusting the sending rate based on loss signals.
QoS mechanisms such as IntServ and DiffServ differentiate traffic for real‑time services.
SCTP combines the best of TCP and UDP while adding multi‑streaming and multi‑homing.
bank_note: Syllabi stress clear definitions, step‑by‑step protocol operations, and the ability to compare TCP and UDP behaviours in exam answers.

bank.q: Define the terms port, multiplexing and demultiplexing in the context of the transport layer.
Explain why UDP is described as connection‑less and list the fields present in a UDP header.
outline: Header fields: Src Port, Dst Port, Length, Checksum

bank.q: A client sends a 1500‑byte message using UDP. Show how the message is divided into UDP datagrams and compute the total header overhead.
outline: Total UDP header bytes (8 bytes per datagram)

bank.q: Illustrate the three‑way handshake with a diagram. Indicate the sequence and acknowledgment numbers for each segment.
A TCP sender has a congestion window of 4 KB and a receiver advertised window of 8 KB. The sender receives three duplicate ACKs. Describe the sender’s next actions.
outline: Fast retransmit of the missing segment
Adjust congestion window as per algorithm

bank.q: Compare TCP and UDP for a live video streaming application. Discuss reliability, latency, bandwidth usage and suitability of each protocol.
Explain how sliding‑window flow control and congestion control work together to avoid network overload. Use a numerical example with window sizes.
outline: Example showing window growth and reduction

bank.q: Discuss the role of Quality of Service (QoS) in supporting real‑time services such as VoIP over a congested network. Mention IntServ and DiffServ briefly.
outline: Effect on jitter and packet loss

bank.q: List and describe the purpose of at least four TCP flags.
Given a TCP segment with Data Offset = 6, calculate the size of the TCP header in bytes.
Explain how SCTP’s multi‑streaming feature can prevent head‑of‑line blocking compared to TCP.
outline: Contrast with TCP’s single byte‑stream ordering

bank.q: A server uses UDP to receive DNS queries. Show how the server distinguishes queries from different clients.
outline: Use of source port in each query
Mapping of (IP, source port) to client state

bank.q: State the purpose of the TCP Urgent Pointer field.
